behavior_constraints: ${steps.STEPNAME.output} resolves to the trimmed stdout of that step after it completes successfully
${steps.STEPNAME.output} resolves to an empty string for failed steps
${steps.STEPNAME.duration} resolves to the wall-clock duration of the step in seconds formatted to two decimal places (e.g., "0.15")
${steps.STEPNAME.duration} is available for all completed steps including failed and skipped ones; skipped steps report duration "0.00"
The new .output and .duration references work wherever ${...} substitution already works: commands, conditions, environment variable values, and default syntax like ${steps.X.output:-fallback}
Existing capture_output mechanism continues to work independently, capturing stdout into a named variable, while .output is always the raw trimmed stdout
entities.summary: This round adds automatic ${steps.STEPNAME.output} (trimmed stdout, empty on failure) and ${steps.STEPNAME.duration} (two-decimal seconds, including for failed/skipped steps) references usable anywhere ${...} substitution works, alongside the existing capture_output mechanism.

instruction_head:
Pipeline steps produce output that currently requires explicit `capture_output` to make available downstream. This is clunky for simple cases — most of the time you just want to reference what a step printed.

Introduce automatic step output and timing references:
- `${steps.STEPNAME.output}` resolves to the trimmed stdout of that step after it completes successfully. For failed steps, the output reference resolves to empty string.
